review_scope: runtime-only binding of an already-qualified restricted DIVDRA projection

invariants.basis: One existing DIVDRA process is called; no alternate kernel or use-case-specific physics is created.
The candidate has no file, path, parser, format or unit I/O dependency.
Parameters, hydraulic view, scalar transfer, published forcing row and diagnostics remain distinct arguments/objects.
No persistent per-column drainage state is introduced.
Process result and diagnostics are automatic call-local temporaries; no solver scratch is attached to a column.
The publication contract is a simple level-by-node array and does not impose an object-heavy storage model.
Publication occurs only after a successful process return and result-shape validation; prebound targets are rejected before evaluation.
The binding is stateless and deterministic for explicit inputs, allowing cheap replay from the same physical state.
No calendar or fixed-duration concept exists in the candidate.
No coupling-window duration or alignment is encoded.
Checkpoint/corrector orchestration is outside this narrow projection binding and is neither bypassed nor modified.
No groundwater-model head/flux interface is implemented by this candidate.
The runtime row is copied bit-for-bit from the qualified process result and the authoritative scalar is not reconstructed, normalized or relaxed.
No response tangent is claimed; derivative/Jacobian work remains outside the admitted restricted scope.
One bounded process projection is added, with no additional full SWAP execution.
No global state or heavyweight per-column solver object is introduced; calls can be issued independently per job/column.
The candidate knows no MODFLOW cell or tile fraction.
Deep-vadose transfer remains external and absent.
No transition between direct and deep-vadose coupling is performed.
Hydraulic information enters through process_hydraulic_view_t rather than any Richards implementation detail.
The admitted DIVDRA process is reused exactly; its physics is not replicated in runtime.
No HeadCalc internals or legacy solver arrays are visible to the binding.
The frozen physical scope is explicit and no numerical policy switch changes drainage physics.
The binding contains no retry loop, adaptive search or unbounded iteration.
Reference-mode availability and implementation are unchanged.
Typed diagnostics report binding status, process status, evaluation/publication state, target shape and authoritative scalar.
Memory for the drainage row is allocated only when the optional binding is invoked and succeeds.
Composition is explicitly performed in runtime while the process remains unaware of backend/system topology.
Hydraulic view and scalar exchange are explicit inputs; no midnight, daily, file-format or MODFLOW dependency is hidden.
This independent qualification explicitly reviews all thirty architecture invariants and machine-checks the critical runtime restrictions.
